{{short description|British surface physicist}}
{{for|persons of a similar name|David Woodruff (disambiguation)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''David Phillip Woodruff ''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] is a British [[physicist]], professor at [[University of Warwick]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/physics/staff/academic/woodruff/ |title=Prof. D. Phil Woodruff FRS |website=Warwick.ac.uk |date=2016-10-04 |access-date=2017-05-22}}</ref> and member of the Surface, Interface & Thin Films group.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/physics/research/condensedmatt/surface/about |title=Research Themes |website=Warwick.ac.uk |date=2013-06-19 |access-date=2017-05-22}}</ref>. He died in 2026 at the age of 81.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alumni in memoriam |url=https://www.bristol.ac.uk/media-library/sites/alumni/documents/in-memoriam-2026.pdf |publisher=University of Bristol |access-date=18 August 2026}}</ref>

== Education ==
He earned a B.Sc. from [[University of Bristol]] in 1965, and a Ph.D.(1968), and D.Sc. (1983) from [[Warwick University]].{{citation needed|date=July 2016}}
He formally retired in 2011,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/physics/events/?calendarItem=094d4392325dc54a01326332c6f56cc7 |title=Events |website=Warwick.ac.uk |date=2011-09-28 |access-date=2017-05-22}}</ref> but remained research active until shortly before his death.<ref>{{cite web |last1=McConville |first1=Chris |last2=Bell |first2=Gavin |last3=Cooper |first3=Malcolm |title=Tribute to Professor D. Phil Woodruff, FRS |url=https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/physics/staff/phil_woodruff/ |website=University of Warwick |access-date=18 August 2026}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
Woorduff is a fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]], and the Woodruff Thesis prize is named in his honour.<ref>{{cite web |title=Group prize |url=http://www.iop.org/activity/groups/subject/tfsg/prize/page_50366.html |access-date=26 December 2019 |publisher=Institute of Physics |archive-date=26 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191226130444/http://www.iop.org/activity/groups/subject/tfsg/prize/page_50366.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He won the [[Nevill Mott Medal and Prize]] in 2003,<ref>{{cite web |title=Nevill Mott medal recipients |url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/subject/mott/mott-medallists/page_38571.html |access-date=26 December 2019 |publisher=Institute of Physics}}</ref> and [[Max Born Medal and Prize]] in 2011. During his career, Woodruff published over 560 scientific articles.<ref>{{cite web |last1=McConville |first1=Chris |last2=Bell |first2=Gavin |last3=Cooper |first3=Malcolm |title=Tribute to Professor D. Phil Woodruff, FRS |url=https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/sci/physics/staff/phil_woodruff/ |website=University of Warwick |access-date=18 August 2026}}</ref>
